Subject: Redwood MSA — treatment of regulatory fines and third-party claims

Diego,

Thanks for the redline — we've reviewed the MSA and have two open items on our side before we can finalize: the treatment of regulatory fines (GDPR/CCPA) and how third-party PCI claims are handled under the Limitation of Liability. Procurement prefers a carve-out for regulatory penalties with an uncapped indemnity, but our legal/privacy team flagged this as high risk for Redwood.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on: (1) unlimited liability for regulatory fines vs. a capped carve-out, and (2) whether third-party PCI assessments will be treated as indemnifiable claims or fall under the overall cap?

We attached the current redline and our preferred wording in the order form. We need a response this week to keep our procurement calendar.

Regards,
Kelly Morris

Subject: Re: Redwood MSA — treatment of regulatory fines and third-party claims

Thanks Kelly — looping in legal: Laura and Rishi can you weigh in on the two asks below?

Quick context for Acme: our standard position is to carve regulatory fines out of the financial cap when they arise from Customer's regulated activities where Redwood materially contributed; for provider-side issues (e.g., breach of our platform) we accept either uncapped indemnity or a high cap (typically 3x annual fees or $5M, whichever is higher) depending on risk profile. For PCI specifically, we generally treat third-party card-scheme fines/assessments as within indemnity if caused by our negligence, but often subject to the overall cap unless an explicit carve-out is negotiated.

Laura/Rishi — recommendation for Acme (large healthcare customer): propose doing an explicit regulatory-fines carve-out but with a reasonableness filter and notification/defense rights. For PCI, suggest an indemnity for third-party claims if Redwood's noncompliance is established, with a higher cap than usual (propose $10M aggregate) and explicit subrogation language.

Diego
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Redwood MSA — treatment of regulatory fines and third-party claims

Kelly / Diego,

Thanks for the note. For clarity — below is redline-friendly language we'd accept and the rationale. Please circulate internally and let us know whether Acme counsel can live with the guardrails.

Proposed language (MSA, Limitation of Liability section):
- Regulatory fines. Notwithstanding any limitation of liability or damages cap in this Agreement, either partyshall not be liable for Regulatory Penalties to the extent resulting from the other party's willful misconduct or gross negligence; provided, however, that Redwood's liability for Regulatory Penalties arising from Redwood's failure to comply with its obligations under this Agreement shall be capped at the greater of (i) three (3) times the fees paid to Redwood in the prior 12 months, or (ii) five million U.S. dollars (USD 5,000,000), except that in the case of fines or penalties stemming from statutory data-protection obligations (e.g., GDPR or CCPA) levied directly against a party by a governmental authority, such fines shall be excluded from this cap if the fines arise from that party's willful or grossly negligent conduct.

- Third-party PCI claims. Redwood agrees to indemnify Customer for third-party claims, damages, fines, or assessments imposed by payment-card networks that are caused by Redwood's failure to implement and maintain PCI controls required under this Agreement, subject to an aggregate cap of ten million U.S. dollars (USD 10,000,000). This indemnity shall not apply to third-party claims arising from Customer's misconfiguration or negligence.

Key guardrails: notice and cooperation rights, Redwood's right to assume defense and control of settlement, and an obligation that Customer mitigate penalties/reasonably cooperate with Redwood's remediation. Also recommend an explicit subrogation clause so Redwood can recover from vendors/vendors' insurers where Redwood was not the proximate cause.

Rishi and Marissa — flagged possible pushback on the uncapped carve-out; the language above tries to preserve Acme's need for protection while giving Redwood financial certainty. If Acme insists on fully uncapped regulatory liability for any statutory fine regardless of fault, that would require exec sign-off.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:13:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA — treatment of regulatory fines and third-party claims

Following up with negotiation posture and fallback options so Diego can discuss with Acme procurement today.

Preferred posture (no exec):
- Accept limited carve-out for regulatory fines where fines stem from Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence; apply cap of max(3x prior 12 months fees, USD 5M).
- For statutory data-protection fines levied directly on Customer (e.g., GDPR), Redwood will not accept uncapped liability if Customer was at fault; propose mutual carve-out language with obligation to cooperate on investigations.

Fallback (requires exec):
- Uncapped carve-out for regulatory fines where governmental penalties are actually assessed against Customer due to Redwood's actionable failure (exec sign-off required; escalate with revenue/opportunity context).

PCI: accept indemnity with USD 10M cap, Redwood to control defense, Customer able to participate with counsel at its own expense. Require proof of PCI scope and that Redwood's environment was in-scope.

Ask of Acme: confirm whether their procurement/legal can accept the cap+reasonableness language; if they need uncapped exposure for all regulatory penalties regardless of cause, provide concrete examples so we can brief execs.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Redwood MSA — treatment of regulatory fines and third-party claims

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Acme legal/counsel reviewed internal and they're prepared to accept the cap language for Redwood-originated fines (3x fees or USD 5M) provided we add: (1) a carve-out for any fines imposed directly on Customer by a regulator where regulator explicitly names Redwood as the party responsible (in which case Acme wants Redwood to assume remediation costs and have no cap), and (2) a short window (30 days) for Redwood to cure/respond before Customer engages public disclosure or remediation that would expand the penalty.

On PCI: the USD 10M cap is acceptable if Redwood will confirm in writing that the services in-scope for PCI are limited to the managed payment connector listed in the Order Form and that Redwood will cooperate with Acme's PCI assessor and provide logs necessary for evidence.

Next steps: Diego, can you confirm acceptance of the two carve-out tweaks above? If so, we'll issue a final sign-off and move to final DocuSign. We attached the PCI-scan-report.pdf for your review.

Kelly Morris
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Health
